name: OpenMediaVault
summary: Open-source network attached storage (NAS) software solution based on Debian GNU/Linux, offering modular web administration, software RAID management, SMB/NFS/FTP shares and Docker container integration.

content.introduction: OpenMediaVault (OMV) is an open-source unified network storage (NAS) solution designed to turn any standard personal computer or server into a centralised file and application server. Originally designed by Volker Theile, a former key developer of the FreeNAS project, OpenMediaVault relies on the Debian GNU/Linux distribution to offer a lightweight, accessible and modular alternative to commercial proprietary NAS systems.
content.what_is_it: Technically, OpenMediaVault comes either in the form of a complete stand-alone installation image based on Debian, or in the form of software packages that can be deployed directly on an existing Debian GNU/Linux installation. The system includes all the services essential to managing a home or small business data centre: disk partitioning, S.M.A.R.T. monitoring, volume aggregation into software RAID, user account management and folder sharing on the local network.
content.storage_services_and_filesystems: OpenMediaVault provides extensive support for the major file systems of the Linux ecosystem, notably ext4 (the file system recommended by default), Btrfs (with snapshot and subvolume management), XFS and JFS, as well as reading and writing on NTFS and exFAT volumes for exchanging removable media. Hard disk fault tolerance is administered through the `mdadm` utility of the Linux kernel (RAID levels 0, 1, 5, 6 and 10) or through the LVM2 logical volume manager. File access takes place through standardised network protocols: SMB/CIFS (through Samba with access control list management), NFS (v3 and v4), FTP/SFTP (ProFTPD) and rsync for scheduled replication.
content.management_architecture_and_webui: The internal architecture of OpenMediaVault rests on a clear separation between the configuration storage layer and the application daemons. The system state is centralised in a declarative XML configuration file (`config.xml`). A background daemon (`omv-engined`) exposes an RPC (Remote Procedure Call) interface and orchestrates the actual configurations of the system services by means of SaltStack automation modules (`omv-salt`). The administrator drives the whole machine from a secure web graphical interface accessible through a simple browser, offering interactive dashboards for monitoring temperatures, hardware failure alerts and network load.
content.modularity_and_docker_containerization: One of the decisive assets of OpenMediaVault is its modularity through plugins. In addition to the official modules (ClamAV antivirus, NUT uninterruptible power supply, BorgBackup backups), the community maintains the OMV-Extras extension repository. This additional layer makes it easy to integrate advanced features such as ZFS support (through ZFS on Linux) and above all complete management of application containers thanks to the `openmediavault-compose` plugin. The latter makes it possible to host dozens of self-hosted services (Plex, Jellyfin, Nextcloud, Home Assistant) through Docker and Docker Compose directly on the NAS server without altering the base operating system.
content.hardware_efficiency_and_sbc_support: Unlike demanding enterprise solutions such as TrueNAS, OpenMediaVault stands out through remarkable hardware frugality. It can run stably with only 1 to 2 GB of RAM and a standard entry-level processor, which makes it a preferred tool for recycling old desktop PCs into storage servers. In addition, thanks to adapted deployment scripts and the Armbian ecosystem, OpenMediaVault is very commonly installed on single-board computers (SBC) such as the Raspberry Pi or Odroid boards, providing a compact and energy-efficient NAS gateway.
content.user_access_control_and_security_permiss: Access to stored data is managed through users, groups and shared-folder permissions before any service sees a request. The documentation describes three permission levels on a shared folder - read/write, read only and no access - applied through group membership, with a note that finer control belongs to the filesystem access control list described in the shared-folder documentation. Users belong to groups, a group identifier must be numeric between 1000 and 60000, and groups can be created in bulk from CSV data, which matters on installations that map an existing directory service. These permissions are enforced by the services themselves, such as SMB/CIFS or FTP, and the documentation presents them as a layer distinct from the underlying filesystem ownership.
content.debian_package_base_and_plugin_model: The product is a Debian system, and the documentation states that base directly: openmediavault is described as a NAS solution built on Debian Linux for x86-64 and ARM, and the system is administered as a Debian installation with the openmediavault packages on top. Extension happens through plugins, which the documentation calls the preferred way to extend the NAS because of the modular design, and third-party plugins are catalogued at omv-extras.org rather than in the main documentation. For software outside that catalogue the guidance is to run containerised applications built with podman or Docker instead of installing regular packages alongside the NAS stack, the stated reason being component dependencies that later updates turn into conflicts and that can leave the web interface unusable. The FAQ lists `omv-upgrade` and `omv-release-upgrade` as the two maintenance commands of the system and points to the software section for their description.
advantages: Very low system footprint and memory consumption, allowing installation on modest or recycled hardware.
Proven foundation based on Debian GNU/Linux guaranteeing exemplary stability and reliable security updates.
Responsive and clear web administration interface, making NAS configuration accessible without in-depth command-line skills.
Highly extensible architecture thanks to the official plugin system and the OMV-Extras community repository.
Smooth integration of Docker and Docker Compose facilitating the self-hosting of containerised applications and services.
Official and community support for the x86-64 and ARM architectures (Raspberry Pi, Odroid) for compact servers.
disadvantages: Advanced features such as ZFS are not integrated into the default kernel and depend on third-party modules or backports.
The web interface takes full control of the configuration of the managed services, which can overwrite any manual modifications made on the command line.
Technical support relies mainly on the community and the official forum, without a direct commercial support contract for large accounts.
System installation monopolises a complete storage disk for the operating system by default when using the official ISO.
Less suited to very large enterprise server fleets or multipath cluster SAN architectures than TrueNAS Enterprise-type solutions.
who_is_it_for: Individuals and computing enthusiasts wishing to build a reliable and versatile home NAS server at reduced cost.
Small businesses, craftspeople and liberal professions needing local network sharing space (SMB/NFS) and automated backup.
Users of single-board computers (Raspberry Pi, ARM SBC) seeking to create a small discreet file and download server.
Self-hosting enthusiasts wishing to manage lightweight Docker containers alongside their data shares.
who_is_it_not_for: Large data centre infrastructures requiring natively integrated clustered distributed file systems (Ceph, GlusterFS) or 24/7 commercial support.
Users looking for a proprietary turnkey storage appliance with integrated hardware after-sales service (Synology, QNAP).
Infrastructures imperatively requiring hardware high availability with active-passive dual controllers without service interruption.
Deployments on individual office workstations requiring a local graphical environment with screen and keyboard.
content.verdict: OpenMediaVault is a free network storage distribution intended for home environments and small structures. Built on Debian GNU/Linux, it provides web administration, a reduced resource footprint and extension through modules and Docker Compose.
content.origine_et_lignee_du_projet:
The chronology published by the project begins with version 0.2, named Ix, based on Debian 6 and dated October 2011. The following versions keep this correspondence with the stable version of Debian: 6.0 Shaitan, on Debian 11, published in May 2022; 7.0 Sandworm, on Debian 12, published in March 2024; 8.0 Synchrony, on Debian 13, published in December 2025 and given as stable in the 8.x documentation.

The version table has four columns: number, code name, base distribution and status, with the release date and the end-of-support date. The end-of-support column gives June 2026 for version 7.0. The code names of versions 4.0 Arrakis, 5.0 Usul and 6.0 Shaitan are taken from the Dune universe; those of the following versions do not follow the same source.

The project describes itself as a network storage solution based on Debian, distributed under the GPLv3 licence, with a modular architecture extended by plugins. The services cited in the official presentation include SSH, (S)FTP, SMB/CIFS, a DAAP multimedia server, RSync and Kubernetes. The 8.x documentation carries the mention of a last update on 2026-06-08.
content.installation_multivariante_et_conditions:
The documentation explicitly excludes installation in LXC or in any other container solution. It distinguishes five variants: installation on a dedicated disk from an ISO image, which is the recommended method on x86-64 or AMD64 hardware; installation on a USB key; installation on an already present Debian system; installation by debootstrap, presented as a last resort when the installer does not recognise an essential component such as an NVMe disk or a recent network card; installation on an SD card. For ARM32 and ARM64 boards, the Debian variant is the one indicated.

At the first boot, the login screen displays the IP address assigned to the web interface. The default identifier is `admin` with the password `openmediavault`; the root password is the one chosen during installation, and on ARM images it is identical to that of the admin account. The documentation specifies that SSH access to the root account is enabled by default in order to allow access to a system without a screen, that it must be disabled on the Services page then SSH, and that root access then goes through an unprivileged user added to the `_ssh` and `sudo` groups, then through `sudo su`.

The installation page of the 8.x documentation carries the mention of a last update on 2025-12-25.

components.name: Debian
components.note: "openmediavault is a free, open-source network attached storage (NAS) solution based on Debian Linux" (openmediavault.org); the historical release table gives Debian 13 as the base distribution of version 8.0 and Debian 12 for 7.0 (docs.openmediavault.org, Releases).

components.name: NGINX
components.note: "What is the default HTTP engine of openmediavault? NGINX. The last version of openmediavault with Apache was 0.5 Sardoukar"; Apache is answered as usable "but is not supported" (FAQ); "The page is delivered using the nginx web server" (Development, How it works).

components.name: PHP
components.note: "Backend PHP code, executes several tasks"; "omv-engined RPC daemon that runs all the PHP backend code. The nginx web server connects to this daemon through the FastCGI PHP socket" (Development, How it works).

components.name: Angular (Angular Material)
components.note: "The web interface, is written in TypeScript using the Angular and Angular Material frameworks" (Development, How it works).

components.name: omv-engined
components.note: "RPC daemon that runs all the PHP backend code. The nginx web server connects to this daemon through the FastCGI PHP socket. If an error appears in the web interface that indicates no connection to the PHP socket means the daemon is not running" (Development, How it works).

components.name: omv-salt
components.note: "Tool to deploy the configuration and services"; when the apply button is pressed, "omv-salt deploy run samba" rewrites /etc/samba/smb.conf and the Samba daemon is restarted (Development, How it works).

relations.name: Debian
relations.note: Reference Linux distribution serving as the fundamental foundation for the operating system and the software packages.

relations.name: TrueNAS
relations.note: Competing network storage platform powered by OpenZFS, more demanding in hardware resources.

relations.name: Proxmox VE
relations.note: Debian-based virtualisation and containerisation platform, often associated or compared for home server infrastructures.

relations.name: DietPi
relations.note: Lightweight distribution for single-board computers integrating an installation script optimised for OpenMediaVault.

variants.name: openmediavault 8.0 Synchrony (stable)
